title: Tokamak plasma control with reinforcement learning
summary: A single neural network controls the magnetic coils of Lausanne’s TCV tokamak and forms plasmas in different configurations (snowflake, ITER-like shape, double droplet). Trained mainly in simulation and then tested on the real machine. Stated limitations: plasma lasts about three seconds and the machine changes from day to day.
organization: Google DeepMind and EPFL Swiss Plasma Center

evidence.tested: On the TCV tokamak the controller produced and held elongated, conventional, negative-triangularity and snowflake configurations, with accurate tracking of location, current and shape, and sustained two separate 'droplet' plasmas.
evidence.unknown: Transfer to larger or reactor-scale devices is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A deep reinforcement-learning architecture learned to command the full set of control coils from high-level objectives.
